note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 23-year-old woman with a few days of progressively worsening, constant severe lower central abdominal pain (≈8/10) with nausea and light vaginal spotting; face-to-face assessment and an up-to-date pregnancy test were recommended.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Severe, constant lower abdominal (pelvic) pain focused midline below the umbilicus for a few days, worsening in intensity (patient rates ~8/10).
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began a few days ago; pain has been progressive and is now worse.
  - Constipation noted last week for ~1 week; reported to be improved this week.
  - Light vaginal bleeding/spotting and a small amount of vaginal discharge noted; last normal menses ~2–3 weeks ago.
  - Patient reported a pregnancy test approximately 1 month ago (no result in record) and agreed to perform a pregnancy test today.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - No specific relieving factors reported. Pain worse over time.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - Nausea without vomiting.
  - No fever reported; no syncope, shoulder-tip pain, or urinary frequency/strong odor reported.
  - Able to eat and perform daily activities; no significant systemic illness reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No vomiting, no reported fever, no urinary retention or dysuria, no prior pregnancies, no prior abdominal surgeries.
  - No documented hemodynamic instability.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions documented.
- Surgical history: none.
- Obstetric/Gynecologic: no prior pregnancies.
- Allergy: Amoxicillin (patient-reported).

Medications:
- Contraception: Implanon (contraceptive implant) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other regular medications reported.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin.

Social History:
- Age: 23 years.
- Occupation: School teacher.
- Lives with husband and his family.
- Smoking/alcohol/drugs: Patient’s answers were unclear regarding alcohol; denies illicit drug use. Tobacco use not clearly documented.

Family History:
- Not documented / no relevant family history mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Not recorded (patient agreed to face-to-face clinic examination; no exam performed during this consultation).

Investigations:
- Pregnancy test: Patient had a pregnancy test ~1 month prior (result not provided); clinician requested a pregnancy test today and advised performing it urgently.
- No imaging or laboratory results available.
- Plan for in-person pelvic/abdominal examination and further investigations (e.g., ultrasound) discussed.

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression:
- Acute severe lower midline pelvic pain with nausea and light vaginal spotting in a reproductive-age woman. Urgent face-to-face assessment and an up-to-date pregnancy test are required to exclude potentially time-sensitive gynecologic diagnoses (e.g., ectopic pregnancy, adnexal torsion, hemorrhagic ovarian cyst).

DDx Integration (brief):
- Ovarian/adnexal torsion — High on DDx list:
  - Supporting: Severe, constant pelvic pain with nausea and progressive worsening.
  - Opposing: Pain described as midline (not clearly unilateral); no exam/imaging yet.
- Ectopic pregnancy — Medium likelihood:
  - Supporting: Vaginal spotting and pelvic pain; recent sexual activity and no recent pregnancy test since pain onset.
  - Opposing: Pregnancy test done ~1 month ago (result unknown); no signs of hemodynamic compromise reported.
- Ruptured/hemorrhagic ovarian cyst — Medium likelihood:
  - Supporting: Acute pelvic pain and spotting can be seen with cyst rupture.
  - Opposing: Onset described as progressive over days rather than sudden; no imaging/exam yet.
- Conflict noted: DDx references recent intercourse timing (4 days) whereas transcript contains ambiguity about timing of intercourse (patient initially said “four weeks ago. four days ago, sorry”) — timing is unclear.

Issue 1: Acute severe lower abdominal/pelvic pain
- Assessment:
  - Acute pelvic pain of uncertain gynecologic vs abdominal origin; urgent exclusion of surgical/obstetric emergencies (adnexal torsion, ectopic pregnancy) is required.
- Plan:
  - Arrange prompt face-to-face clinical assessment with abdominal and pelvic examination (patient agreed; instructed to call support line to book).
  - Perform a point-of-care or laboratory pregnancy test today; if pregnancy test is positive → urgent review/ED referral for assessment of ectopic pregnancy.
  - If clinical suspicion for adnexal torsion or if exam concerning → urgent pelvic ultrasound (transvaginal/transabdominal) and gynecology/surgical referral.
  - Safety-netting: patient advised to seek earlier review if pain acutely worsens, becomes intolerable, if vomiting prevents oral intake, if faintness/syncope occurs, or if signs of infection/fever develop.

Issue 2: Vaginal bleeding/spotting and discharge
- Assessment:
  - Light irregular bleeding and small discharge in patient with Implanon; differential includes contraceptive-related irregular bleeding, threatened/ectopic pregnancy, ruptured ovarian cyst, PID.
- Plan:
  - Pregnancy test today (urgent).
  - Perform pelvic examination and cervical/vaginal swabs during face-to-face visit as clinically indicated to assess for PID or other causes.
  - Consider pelvic ultrasound to evaluate adnexa and uterus if bleeding/pain pattern or exam suggests intra‑pelvic pathology.
  - Provide STI testing/treatment as indicated based on exam and swab results.

Issue 3: Recent constipation (resolved)
- Assessment:
  - Constipation last week reported, now improved; unlikely to fully explain current severe, constant pelvic pain but remains in differential.
- Plan:
  - No specific treatment documented in this consult; reassess bowel symptoms at face-to-face visit.
  - If gastrointestinal cause suspected on exam, arrange appropriate investigations and symptomatic management.

General plan items:
- Patient to contact support line to arrange in-person clinic appointment; clinician to proceed based on face-to-face findings.
- Repeat pregnancy test today; if positive or if concerning exam findings → urgent gynecology/ED referral.
- No medications prescribed during this consultation; allergy to amoxicillin documented — avoid prescribing β-lactam if allergy confirmed.
- Provide safety-netting advice as above.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (none recorded).
  - Results of prior pregnancy test not documented.
  - No physical examination findings or imaging/lab results available.
  - No documented dose/route/frequency for Implanon (implant recorded without detail) — noted as “dose/route/frequency not documented.”
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - Minor inconsistency regarding timing of recent intercourse (transcript ambiguous; DDx references both 4 days and 4 weeks) — conflict noted.
  - Otherwise DDx and transcript are consistent in highlighting need to exclude ectopic pregnancy and adnexal torsion.
- Transcript quality:
  - Some patient responses were unclear/ambiguous (timing of intercourse, alcohol use); occasional inaudible exchanges noted.
